meta.name: Lunora Astro Input Definitions
meta.purpose: Defines the canonical machine-readable structure, normalization boundaries and validation contract for calculated sky data consumed by astroRules.json.
meta.important_note: This file defines input structure and validation semantics only. It does not contain astrological scoring weights and must never become a second source of scoring truth.

engine_contract.canonical_input_policy: Production scoring must use structured canonical fields generated by the sky-calculation layer.
engine_contract.legacy_text_policy: Legacy or display strings must not be parsed inside the production scoring pipeline. If legacy migration is required, normalize those values in a separate adapter before they reach this contract.
engine_contract.date_semantics: date represents the local calendar date in the supplied timezone.
engine_contract.interval_semantics: All time intervals use half-open boundaries: start_at is inclusive and end_at is exclusive.
engine_contract.event_id_policy: Every underlying astronomical event must have a deterministic stable event_id that remains unchanged across recalculation or refresh of the same event.
engine_contract.unknown_value_policy: Unknown or unsupported canonical values must not produce a rule match or score. Preserve them only as validation diagnostics; never infer or guess a replacement.

moon_phase_input.selection_rule: Select the period satisfying start_at <= recommendation_timestamp < end_at.
moon_phase_input.coverage_rule: moon_phase_periods must provide exactly one active Moon phase for every timestamp covered by the daily input.
moon_phase_input.display_value_policy: Any user-facing Moon phase name must be generated from the selected canonical phase. Display text must never be used as the scoring input.

moon_sign_input.selection_rule: Select the period satisfying start_at <= recommendation_timestamp < end_at.
moon_sign_input.coverage_rule: moon_sign_periods must provide exactly one active Moon sign for every timestamp covered by the daily input.
moon_sign_input.display_value_policy: Any user-facing Moon sign name must be generated from the selected canonical sign. Display text must never be used as the scoring input.

validation: planet_1 and planet_2 must be different canonical planets.
planet pair matching is unordered.
aspect_type must be an exact canonical aspect type; labels such as supportive or hard are not valid aspect types.
start_at must be earlier than end_at.
exact_at must identify the exact pass represented by this event.
A repeated aspect caused by retrograde motion must be represented as separate exact-pass events with separate deterministic event_ids.
The active interval must be calculated by the centralized aspect activation policy; individual aspect rules must not invent their own orb windows.
phase must not be stored as a fixed property of the full event interval. It is derived for the recommendation timestamp.
Display text must not be used to reconstruct missing astronomical fields.

phase_derivation.exact: recommendation_timestamp is within the centrally configured exactness tolerance around exact_at

aspect.orb_policy: The activation orb belongs to the centralized aspect_activation_policy, not to individual event records.
aspect.current_orb_policy: Do not persist a single orb_deg value for the entire event interval. If a future scoring model needs current orb strength, calculate current_orb_deg for the recommendation timestamp.

validation: status must belong to the declared status_family.
Sun and Moon must not be emitted with retrograde, stationary_retrograde or stationary_direct status.
A planet may simultaneously have one motion status and one solar_proximity status.
Mutually exclusive statuses from the same family must not overlap for the same planet.
cazimi, combust and under_the_beams must not overlap as simultaneously active solar_proximity states for the same timestamp.
start_at must be earlier than end_at.
stationary intervals must be produced by one centralized station-detection policy.
under_the_beams may be represented by the calculation layer but currently produces no Lunora score.
planet_status.baseline_policy: Direct motion is the normal baseline and does not need to be emitted as a celestial event for scoring.

validation: condition must be a supported canonical lunar condition.
start_at must be earlier than end_at.
VOC start and end times must be produced by one centralized lunar calculation policy.
The recommendation timestamp must satisfy start_at <= recommendation_timestamp < end_at for the condition to be active.

eclipse.activation_policy: Determine whether the recommendation timestamp falls inside the eclipse window by combining exact_at with the centralized eclipse_activation_window_policy.
validation: event must be solar_eclipse or lunar_eclipse.
exact_at must be the exact astronomical eclipse timestamp.
Do not persist independent window_start_at or window_end_at values in the event record.
Solar and lunar eclipse activation windows must come from the single centralized production policy.
eclipse.production_requirement: eclipse_activation_window_policy must be finalized before eclipse rules are enabled in production.

moon_next_aspect.persistence_policy: Derive at recommendation time. Do not store moon_next_aspect as an independent celestial event.
moon_next_aspect.selection_rule: First identify the Moon's actual chronologically next major applying aspect among all candidate planets and aspect types. An earlier Moon aspect must never be skipped merely because it does not classify as benefic_supportive or malefic_hard.
moon_next_aspect.non_matching_next_aspect_policy: If the Moon's actual next major aspect does not satisfy either classification, return no moon_next_aspect scoring signal. Do not skip it and search for a later classifiable aspect.
moon_next_aspect.sign_boundary_policy: The treatment of applications across a Moon sign boundary must be defined by one centralized lunar application policy and must remain consistent with the engine's moon_void_of_course calculation policy.

output.source_event_id: event_id of the underlying Moon aspect

moon_next_aspect.deduplication: If source_event_id also activates a specific Moon-planet aspect rule, do not score the generic moon_next_aspect rule separately for that same underlying astronomical event.

aspect_activation_contract.single_calculator_rule: All aspect events must be generated by one centralized astronomy calculation layer.
aspect_activation_contract.activation_rule: An aspect event is active only when the recommendation timestamp falls inside the aspect interval calculated by the centralized aspect orb policy.
aspect_activation_contract.phase_rule: Applying, exact and separating state must be derived consistently from the same underlying aspect pass and recommendation timestamp.
aspect_activation_contract.default_phase_scoring: If an astroRules aspect match does not explicitly require a phase, applying, exact and separating states may all match while the aspect event is active.
aspect_activation_contract.input_conjunction_policy: Conjunction events may exist in normalized sky data even when pair-specific conjunction scoring is deferred.
aspect_activation_contract.scoring_policy: The presence of an aspect in normalized input does not itself imply a score. Only a matching active rule in astroRules.json may produce scoring.
aspect_activation_contract.event_identity_rule: Every exact aspect pass must have its own deterministic event_id. Repeated exact passes caused by retrograde motion are separate astronomical events.

astronomical_validation.aspect_geometry_rule: Aspect validity must be calculated from geocentric longitude separation and the centralized configured orb. Nominal aspect geometry and allowed orb must not be inferred from display labels.

geocentric_inner_planet_constraints.note: Do not generate exact Sun-Mercury sextile, square, trine or opposition events.
Do not generate exact Sun-Venus sextile, square, trine or opposition events.
Do not generate exact Mercury-Venus square, trine or opposition events.

astronomical_validation.impossible_event_policy: An astronomically impossible exact aspect configuration must be rejected during sky-data validation and must never reach astroRules matching.

routing_policy.planet_pair_normalization: Normalize both planets to canonical names and order the pair deterministically according to canonical_vocabulary.planets before comparison.
routing_policy.aspect_match: Match the normalized planet pair and exact aspect_type. The aspect event must also be active at the recommendation timestamp. Phase is considered only when the rule explicitly requires a phase.
routing_policy.moon_phase_match: Select the active moon_phase_period at the recommendation timestamp and match its canonical phase to rule.match.moon_phase.
routing_policy.moon_sign_match: Select the active moon_sign_period at the recommendation timestamp and match its canonical sign to rule.match.moon_sign.
routing_policy.planet_status_match: Match the canonical planet and status to rule.match.planet and rule.match.status. status_family is used for input validation and does not create an additional score unless a rule explicitly requests it.
routing_policy.lunar_condition_match: Match the canonical condition only while its event interval is active at the recommendation timestamp.
routing_policy.eclipse_match: Match the canonical eclipse event only when the recommendation timestamp falls inside the single centralized configured eclipse activation window.
routing_policy.moon_next_aspect_match: Match the derived moon_next_aspect signal to rule.match.moon_next_aspect only after moon-next-aspect derivation and source-event deduplication are complete.
routing_policy.wildcard_planet_match: A rule value of planet='*' may match a canonical planet only after all rule-specific and input-validation eligibility constraints have passed.
routing_policy.replacement_policy_source: Eclipse and lunar-phase replacement behavior must come from astroRules.json, not from this input-definition file.
routing_policy.unknown_or_ambiguous_input: Produce no score and record a validation diagnostic. Never guess the intended canonical value.

deduplication_policy.same_underlying_event: The same underlying astronomical event must retain the same deterministic event_id across recalculation and refresh.
deduplication_policy.derived_signal_identity: A derived signal must reference the event_id of the astronomical event from which it was derived. It must not create a second independent astronomical event identity.
deduplication_policy.moon_next_aspect_double_count_policy: If the source_event_id of a moon_next_aspect signal also activates a specific Moon-planet aspect rule, score the specific aspect rule and do not separately score the generic moon_next_aspect rule for that same source_event_id.
deduplication_policy.repeated_exact_pass_policy: Separate exact passes of the same planet pair and aspect type caused by retrograde or direct motion must use separate deterministic event_ids.
deduplication_policy.replacement_behavior_source: Rule replacement and deduplication such as eclipse versus ordinary lunar phase must be controlled by astroRules.json and must not be duplicated in this input-definition file.

timestamp_validation.interval_rule: For every interval, start_at must be earlier than end_at.
timestamp_validation.interval_boundary_semantics: Use half-open intervals: start_at is inclusive and end_at is exclusive.

daily_period_validation.daily_coverage_rule: moon_sign_periods and moon_phase_periods must cover the complete local calendar day represented by date, from local 00:00 inclusive to the next local 00:00 exclusive.

error_scope_policy.daily_input_error: If required daily structure, timezone, Moon-sign coverage or Moon-phase coverage is invalid, do not use that daily input for recommendation scoring.
error_scope_policy.individual_event_error: If one celestial event is invalid but the rest of the daily input is valid, quarantine that event and continue scoring from the remaining valid inputs.
error_scope_policy.valid_but_unmatched_event: Keep the valid event for diagnostics if useful, but produce no astrological score when no active astroRules rule matches it.

validation_policy.unknown_or_ambiguous_input_policy: Never guess or infer a canonical scoring value from incomplete or ambiguous data.

required_fixes_in_current_astroRules_bef.reason: The active relevant_planet_direct rule has been removed, so this stale cap no longer has a producer.
A geocentric Mercury-Venus trine cannot occur. The active rule must contain sextile only.
